title: ticket_inspector reads a clause-shaped falsifier as structured
intention: ticket_inspector's falsifier_structure check passes a falsifier object carrying clauses [{n, claim}] numbered 1..k, and names the lack when clauses is malformed, while the standing {proves_green, proves_red} and string shapes read as before.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py:137-144: a dict falsifier is red unless it carries proves_green and proves_red, so every ticket the parent's door admits would red here. The parent e4f02a1ceef5 makes the ticket plan JSON at the cast door (Akien 2026-11-05: 'should be json'); this reader must read the new shape before the door admits it.
traces_to: Law 4 and Law 1 via parent e4f02a1ceef5; RULE 1 (each reader's change lives in its own component).
how: In the FALSIFIER STRUCTURE block, a dict carrying 'clauses' is judged by clauses (list, each {n:int, claim:non-blank}, n = 1..k) instead of proves_green/proves_red; red-first proof.
falsifier: (1) a ticket whose falsifier is {clauses: [{n:1, claim:'x'}, {n:2, claim:'y'}]} yields no falsifier_structure finding; (2) clauses empty, a blank claim, or numbering [1, 3] each yields one falsifier_structure finding naming it; (3) a {proves_green, proves_red} falsifier and a string falsifier yield exactly what they yield at HEAD.

decisions.text: Red-first proof cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/proofs/test_a_clause_shaped_falsifier_is_structured.py, check()/FAILURES/main() shape, one tooth per falsifier clause, PROVES = {'660352d41cb7': {'1': 'clause_1', '2': 'clause_2', '3': 'clause_3'}} (tooth names written at build, each named for its clause). Red at HEAD on the new-shape teeth.
